methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon's cancellation of four NoVA data centers due to local backlash signals infrastructure saturation in the dominant hub without corresponding capability distribution to other regions, reinforcing concentration limits while other areas remain underserved.

signals.title: Roanoke coalition names Texas firm to study AI center plan - Virginia Business
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke's coalition hiring consultants to study an AI Center of Excellence represents intentional grassroots capability-building outside traditional tech hubs, potentially creating deep distributed expertise if the center materializes with workforce development focus.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: A governor-ordered statewide AI cybersecurity plan signals policy recognition of AI risks but originates from Richmond/NoVA power centers, likely to concentrate defensive expertise in already-capable state agencies rather than distributing security literacy broadly.

signals.title: Roanoke County Career and Technology Center opens - WSLS
signals.signal_reading: Opening of Roanoke County's Career and Technology Center provides infrastructure for distributed technical workforce development, potentially enabling peer-to-peer AI fluency outside metro hubs if curriculum evolves beyond traditional trades to include emerging technology skills.

signals.title: AI breast cancer tools show promise but still need work - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: AI breast cancer detection tools in Hampton Roads healthcare show platform-delivered shallow adoption—clinicians using AI without deep technical understanding, creating broad but surface-level capability tied to vendor solutions rather than local innovation capacity.
